title: Bilinear Forms behind Resistor and Ising Integrable Equations
exact_target: Explain conceptually why symmetric and antisymmetric projective bilinear forms produce the indicated resistor/Ising and BKP/CKP pairings.

sources.citation: ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, UnsolvedMath, record 30004562 (OWR-2654831-005). Catalogue curation under CC BY 4.0; definitions and English exposition added locally.

Mini-Workshop: Dimers, Ising and Spanning Trees beyond the Critical Isoradial Case (2020), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2020/35, pp. 1759--1789. Primary report accessed 2026-10-11; relevant PDF pages 22.
Affolter, discrete differential geometry and cluster algebras (catalogue-listed context; not independently consulted in this preparation).

status_qualification: The relevant subvarieties, diagram maps and integrable equations are source-defined, not arbitrary bilinear forms on arbitrary vector spaces. The question asks for the mechanism behind the reported examples, not simply verification of their names.
